title: kate-search: skip a find for an empty escape
summary: find_next returns Ok(None) when an escape pattern expands to empty text. find_all still reports the empty spans. An invalid escape still returns the error. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition:
pub fn find_next(
    buf: &TextBuffer,
    q: &SearchQuery,
    from: Offset,
    backwards: bool,
    wrap: bool,
) -> Result<Option<Match>, SearchError>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: In find_next, after the empty Plain check, match Pattern::EscapeSequences. Call escape::expand_pattern. When that call returns Ok and the string is empty, return Ok(None). When that call returns Err, return the error. A non-empty expansion still searches. The empty Plain check stays as it is. find_all stays as it is for an empty escape pattern. Leave bar.rs and escape.rs unchanged. The test an_empty_escape_pattern_returns_none uses the buffer abc and Pattern::EscapeSequences of an empty string. find_all still returns four empty spans at 0, 1, 2, and 3. find_next from offset 0 with backwards false and wrap false returns None. A plain pattern a from offset 0 still returns the hit 0..1. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep this change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: find_tests::an_empty_escape_pattern_returns_none
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. find_next returns a hit at offset 1 for an empty escape pattern. After the change it returns None. find_all still returns four empty spans. A plain pattern a still returns the hit 0..1.
